en: Dependent on a non-material phenomenon, a non-material phenomenon arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a non-material phenomenon, a non-non-material phenomenon arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a non-material phenomenon, both non-material and non-non-material phenomena arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on a non-material phenomenon, a non-material phenomenon arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a non-material phenomenon, a material phenomenon arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a non-material phenomenon, both material and non-material phenomena arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on both non-material and non-non-material phenomena, a non-material phenomenon arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on both non-material and non-non-material phenomena, a non-non-material phenomenon arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on both non-material and non-non-material phenomena, both non-material and non-non-material phenomena arise by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of the root condition, there are nine; in the object condition, three; in the predominance condition, five …pe… in the mutuality condition, six …pe… in the prenascence and repetition conditions, one …pe… in the non-disappearance condition, nine.
(The same applies in the section on conascence …pe… and in the section on inquiry, with full detail in all instances.)
